newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA STUDENTS PROTEST SUBSIDY CUTS, ECON PLAN.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA STUDENTS PROTEST SUBSIDY CUTS, ECON PLAN.

text.p: South African students on Wednesday marched on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange to protest against state subsidy cuts at universities and colleges and to urge business to help them pay escalating study fees.

Addressing a crowd of about 1,000 students in the centre of Johannesburg, the South African Students Congress (Sasco) also said that government had abandoned them, evident in the state's five-year economic plan.

"The Growth, Employment and Redistribution programme is non-negotiable. We reject that programme as it has a neo-liberal paradigm," said Jacob Mamabolo, Sasco chairperson in the populous Gauteng province.

The plan, unveiled in June last year by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel, aims to raise the country's economic growth rate to 6.1 percent by the year 2000, creating hundreds of thousands of jobs every year reaching 400,000 by the turn of the century.

Mamabola said government in drawing up the plan had not asked for any input from Sasco, nor any of its allies, including the South African Communist Party and the Congress of South African Trade Unions.

Sasco handed over a memorandum containing their grievences to JSE Acting President Bill Urman before proceeding to the provincial government to present a similar document to Jabu Moleketi, Gauteng's head of finance and economic affairs.

South African university and college campuses have in recent years been rocked by protests from students unable to pay escalating fees. Institutions, many which have been crippled by millions of rands of outstanding fees, face further subsidy cuts this year.
